o.text: Internationalism. Ultimately from Ancient Greek λεξικόν (lexikón).

From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (yeke, “large”), from Middle Mongol ᠶᠡᠬᠡ (yeke), from Proto-Mongolic *jeke whence also Modern Mongolian их (ix, “great”).
Attested since the 13th century.
Internationalism; likely via Russian автограф (avtograf), from Latin autographum, ultimately from Ancient Greek αὐτόγραφος (autógraphos).
From Classical Persian حاکمیت (hākimiyyat), from Arabic حَاكِمِيَّة (ḥākimiyya).
Izafet II compound of dil (“language”) + daşıyıcı (“carrier”). Calque of Russian носи́тель языка́ (nosítelʹ jazyká).

From yox + -al.
Cognates
* Kazakh жоғалу (joğaluw, “to get lost”)
* Kyrgyz жоголуу (jogoluu, “to disappear, to get lost”)
* Uzbek yoʻqolmoq (“get lost”)
* Uyghur يوقالماق (yoqalmaq, “to get lost, disappear”)
* Turkish yoğalmak (“to disappear”)
* Turkmen ýogalmak (“to disappear, die”)
